pages.title: EOS-05 on GSLV-F17 — first imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit

facts.text: Launched: 4 September 2026, GSLV-F17, Second Launch Pad, SDSC-SHAR Sriharikota
facts.head: Mission

facts.text: ⚠ India's first imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit
facts.head: Mission

facts.text: Mass: ~2,367 kg; placed in Sub-GTO (perigee 170 km, apogee 28,934 km, inclination 19.28°, azimuth 104°) — not directly in GEO
facts.head: Mission

facts.text: 19th GSLV flight; height 51.7 m; lift-off mass 420.5 t; 3 stages; 4 m ogive fairing
facts.head: GSLV-F17

facts.text: Stage: GS1; Detail: S139 solid core + 4 L40H liquid strap-ons
facts.head: GSLV-F17

facts.text: Stage: GS2; Detail: GL40HT liquid stage
facts.head: GSLV-F17

facts.text: Stage: GS3; Detail: CUS15 cryogenic (LH2 + LOX)
facts.head: GSLV-F17

facts.text: GSLV Mk II capacity: ~2,250 kg to GTO, 6,000 kg to LEO; first flight 18 April 2001; indigenous cryo stage from GSLV-D5 (January 2014)
facts.head: GSLV-F17

facts.text: LEO 160–2,000 km (orbit 90–120 min) — ~15,562 active payloads (Sept 4, 2026); India has 22 operational LEO satellites (April 2026 ISRO report)
facts.head: Orbits background

facts.text: Geosynchronous period ~23 h 56 min — may be elliptical/inclined; geostationary — circular, equatorial, zero inclination, ~35,786 km; India has 31 GEO satellites
facts.head: Orbits background

facts.text: Galileo (Europe): 30 satellites in MEO
facts.head: Orbits background

facts.text: CA-360: EOS-05 also called GISAT-1A; images subcontinent every 30 min (priority areas ~5 min) from ~36,000 km
facts.head: Orbits background

facts.text: Uses: agriculture, land resources, environmental and weather monitoring, disaster management
facts.head: CA-360 extras

facts.text: ⚠ Unlike LEO/Sun-Synchronous EO satellites, it watches the same large area with very high temporal frequency
facts.head: CA-360 extras

facts.text: Geostationary orbit: ~35,786 km above the equator; period ~24 hours; appears stationary — used for communications, weather, continuous regional monitoring
facts.head: CA-360 extras

facts.text: SDSC: Sriharikota, AP — ISRO's principal launch centre; former name Sriharikota Range; named after Prof. Satish Dhawan
facts.head: CA-360 extras
